thread:
kai: heads-up — observed a ~12% p50 token latency regression on SM90 for the paged+flash variant after the kernel-selector change this morning. looks like it picks a different Flash mix under certain seq-distros.

mira: ack. can you paste the run id / input distribution?

kai: run id r-2026-03-17-flashmix. workload: batch sizes mostly 4-8, seq range 256-1536, heavy long-tail around 1024-1280.

sam: interesting — our selector change preferred the fused-attn-triton kernel for >1024 but kept cuda-flash for <1024. that could explain the tail.

jia: do we have nvprof/nsys output showing SM utilization / l2 traffic?

kai: grabbed a quick nsight capture. highlights: kernel `flash_fused_v2` has 15% higher achieved occupancy on SM90 vs SM80, but memory stalls and serialization jump for seq=1280. paste snippet:

```
# from nsys summary
kernel: flash_fused_v2  | duration: 12.4ms | sm_eff: 0.78 | l2_read: 1.9GB | l2_write: 0.6GB | mem_stall_cycles: 23%
kernel: triton_paged_attn | duration: 10.9ms | sm_eff: 0.62 | l2_read: 2.4GB | mem_stall_cycles: 12%
```

mira: so flash_fused is faster on smaller seqs but degrades at long seq due to larger working set and cache thrash. triton_paged looks steadier.

perf-bot: perf regression alert: +12% p50 (service: hosted-inference, model: mix-7b, variant: paged+flash, arch: sm90) — compare to baseline 1850100000.

alex: do we have the kernel selection heuristics in the config that triggered this? I thought we gated by seq*batch tokens and by available VRAM.

sam: the recent change (PR #3109) added a new cost-model that biases toward the highest throughput kernel measured on short synthetic microbenchmarks. it missed the long-tail perf impact.

jia: can we reproduce with the small perf harness? try `make perf-run` with `SEQ=1280 BATCH=6` across both sm80/sm90 and with `USE_TRITON=1/0` flags.

kai: ran that locally — attached logs (cut):

```
# sm90, fused-flash selected
BATCH=6 SEQ=1280 USE_TRITON=0 -> p50=11.9ms p95=28.3ms
# sm90, prefer triton paged
BATCH=6 SEQ=1280 USE_TRITON=1 -> p50=10.7ms p95=18.9ms
# sm80, fused-flash selected
BATCH=6 SEQ=1280 USE_TRITON=0 -> p50=10.8ms p95=19.1ms
```

mira: confirms arch-delta: fused-flash is fine on sm80 but regresses on sm90 for big seqs. likely kernel has SM90-specific code-path (new tensorcore tiling) that increases L2 pressure.

alex: possible quick mitigation: change selector to prefer `triton_paged_attn` for seq >= 1024 on sm90, or add a microbenchmark that includes long-seq synthetic inputs.

sam: I can push a conservative override rule: if arch == sm90 && seq >= 1024 && batch <= 8 -> prefer paged_triton. quick PR in 20m.

jia: also worth adding an instrumentation tag when we pick fused-flash so we can collect live nvstats (l2 utilization, dram bw) from a random 1% of requests for 24h. helps validate.

kai: agree. let's do both: selector override + sampling telemetry. add a short-term rollout (canary 10%) and watch p50/p95.

perf-bot: created perf job r-2026-03-17-canary with selector-override.

ops-bot: scheduled canary on cluster-gpu-sm90-a (10% traffic) at 03:20 UTC. will rollback on error > 2% error rate or latency regressions >5%.

mira: later follow-up — we should also add a small kernel mem-affinity check: when choosing fused-flash, estimate per-block working set (KV cache footprint + attn scratch) and skip fused path if estimated L2 footprint > threshold for sm90. that keeps decision heuristic portable.

sam: noted. I'll prototype estimator in the selector module. estimate formula sketch: est_l2_bytes = kv_active_pages*page_size + attn_tiles*tile_bytes. keep it simple.

alex: one more thing — check CUDA versions. we saw slightly different kernel schedules between 12.2 and 12.3 on sm90 in earlier runs. ensure canary nodes pinned to same driver.

kai: pinned drivers to 12.3 on canary. will post results in ~2h. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

mira: can we make a follow-up doc for the selector introspection? quick notes in the perf runbook would be good.

sam: will open a short RFC/issue and link to this thread.

kai: update — 1h in, p50 on canary dropped back to baseline, p95 improved too. looks promising. will keep monitoring until 24h.

alex: awesome. when stable let's fold the estimator into default policy and add unit microbench with long seqs to CI.

kai: agreed. thanks team.
